text.p: Mediterranean oil products rallied on Monday, boosted variously by gains in crude, a tighter NWE market and stronger futures, trader said.
Naphtha prices ended $3 higher after further gains in crude oil, but traders said the market was balanced and crude's volatility was discouraging cargo trading.
Cargoes ended at $219/$222 cif with fob prices at a $15 discount.
"It's quiet," said one Med trader. "It's following the crude but it is difficult to take a position with the volatility."
Gasoline prices also rallied after the sharp gains in the U.S. on Friday and a tighter NWE market, traders said.
Premium unleaded cargoes rose $5 to $234/$236 cif.
Gas oil was bolstered by stronger futures and heavy demand for Russian heating oil spurred by Greek and Turkish tenders, traders said.

Turkey's state oil company awarded tenders for the supply of at least 75,000 tonnes of heating oil in the second half of November. Tempotrade won an award to supply two cargoes of 25,000 tonnes at mean fob quotes +$10.50 for delivery between November 20-22 and November 30 to December 2.
Onyx won an award to supply a 25,000 tonne cargo at mean fob quotes +$12.85 for delivery November 19-23.
Firmer crude from Friday bolstered low sulphur cracked prices higher to mirror swaps numbers talked around $124 fob NWE, but gave little support to high sulphur cracked cargoes.
"High sulphur was seen a touch overvalued against NWE last week, so the spread has now eased because NWE has risen up," said one Med trader.
Bunker quality material was required into Gibraltar, but supplies were seen from Greece and possibly Syria. "It's essentially fairly balanced," said one trader.
